title: Cold rebuild: umask, a shared folder and an ACL
summary: Set a umask, a setgid team folder and an ACL entry on a real machine, from memory.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *Owners, sudo and umask* you set a default umask, made a setgid team folder and
shared one file with an ACL, on a real machine. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no
solution to peek at**. The checks are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; typing them cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: `sudo echo "10.0.0.5 db" >> /etc/hosts` says *Permission denied*. Which fixes it?
steps.explain: `>>` is performed by your unprivileged shell before sudo runs. `tee` runs under sudo and opens the file itself. Option 2 has the same bug *and* would truncate the file.
